subject: Post-demo recap — projected monthly tokens, budget bracket, and peak TPS window
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@celohealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@celohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — projected monthly tokens, budget bracket, and peak TPS window

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so our pricing/engineering teams can lock in a hosted proposal.

Takeaways from the demo:
- You liked the prefix-caching example and the burst-protection policies.
- Primary use case: real-time summarization for clinician notes + a downstream classification pass for triage.
- Early plan: hosted API (no private deployment initially), potential move to Dedicated at 6–9 months if latency/budget requires.

Requests we need answered to finalize an initial $/1M token target: (short answers ok)
1) Expected steady-state monthly token volume (best guess range). Example: 5–15M / 15–50M / 50–150M.
2) Peak TPS and typical burst window (how long does the peak last?): e.g., 80 TPS for 2 hours, 200 TPS for 15 minutes, etc.
3) Percent of calls that will be streaming vs single-response (streaming increases latency sensitivity).
4) Any hard budget target for $/1M tokens or monthly spend range we should hit for procurement.

Attachment: CeloHealth-MAP-v1.pdf — I captured the mutual action plan from today (stub).

If you can reply inline with short bullets we'll turn it into a hosted rate card and send back a draft SOW by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Grace
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Note: forwarded internal line for visibility: adding Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (AM).

From: Alex Rivera <alex@celohealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@celohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — projected monthly tokens, budget bracket, and peak TPS window

Grace — great demo, thanks. Answers below (rounded):

1) Steady-state monthly tokens: we expect ~25M tokens/month within first 3 months; growth path to 60–80M over 12 months if pilot converts. So for an initial commitment band please assume 20–30M.
2) Peak TPS: typical daytime peak 90–130 TPS; we see a couple of daily spikes tied to EHR ingest windows — worst-case 180–220 TPS but only for ~20–30 minutes. We also have one weekly batch window (30–45 minutes) where simulated throughput can touch ~300 TPS but that's non-production testing.
3) Streaming: roughly 18% of requests will use streaming (real-time transcripts), remaining 82% are single-response summarization/classification calls.
4) Budget target: Procurement wants to keep host spend in the $30k–$45k/month bracket during pilot. That implies a target of ~$40/1M tokens (we're flexible if caching/quantization lowers effective token bill).

Let me know if you need breakdowns by endpoint type (summarize vs classify vs embeddings). Happy to share sample traffic traces.

— Alex
Head of Product | CeloHealth
alex@celohealth.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@celohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@celohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — projected monthly tokens, budget bracket, and peak TPS window

Thanks Alex — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying bullets so the proposal maps to your ops: 

- For hosted rate modeling we'll create two pricing scenarios: (A) conservative: 20–30M tokens/month, targeting $42/1M; (B) upside: 50–80M, targeting $31/1M with reserved-burst credits.
- Peak SLOs: for daytime peaks ~120 TPS we can comfortably meet 99th-percentile latency targets on hosted. For the 180–300 TPS transient windows we recommend an autoscale + short burst policy — confirm if you want automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant when we hit sustained >200 TPS.
- Streaming multiplier: treat streaming requests as 1.6x token-resource weight for initial sizing (we'll refine after traces).
- Procurement check: if your $30k–$45k/mo target is firm for the pilot, scenario (A) is the conservative fit; scenario (B) would require a multi-month commit to hit $31/1M.

Next steps: Karthik will produce a draft hosted rate card and a short-run cost model by tomorrow EOD; Marissa will follow with a one-pager procurement checklist and a proposed SOW cadence. Can you confirm whether the weekly 300 TPS test window should be treated as "test-only" (exclude from SLO) or "production-like" (we size for it)?

Grace
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@celohealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@celohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — projected monthly tokens, budget bracket, and peak TPS window

Quick reply from procurement side — thanks Grace/Karthik/Marissa.
- The weekly 300 TPS window is strictly a non-prod test; exclude it from production SLO sizing.
- $30k–$45k/month is the pilot oval; if Redwood can model a $38k mid-band with a clear point when we convert to reserved/dedicated (based on sustained 60M tokens), procurement will greenlight a 3-month pilot.
- Please include invoicing cadence options (monthly vs net-30 with PO) in the SOW.

We'll expect your draft rate card and SOW by tomorrow; happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk procurement through the billing items.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
VP of Finance | CeloHealth
priya.shah@celohealth.com
